lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Md. Anwar Hossain Raza Advocates ------ For the Petitioners 
Md Mofazzal Hossain with Md Israfil Hossain, Advocates ------ For the Opposite-Parties
parties:
Pear Ahmed and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Tayebur Nessa alias Badunessa and others ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-35 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 11-9-2006 passed by the District Judge, Comilla in Title Appeal No.196 of 1997 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 24-8-1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla in Civil Suit No. 132 of 1994 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the petitioner Nos. 1-2, 12-14 and the predecessor of the petitioner Nos.3-11 as plaintiffs instituted Civil Suit No. 118 of 1988 subsequently (re-numbered as Civil Suit No. 132 of 1994) before the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla for declaration of Title alleging that the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian No.11 corresponding to Hal Khatian No. 40 of Mouja Porkara under Police Station Chowddagram originally belonged to Dula Mia and his brother namely-Sekandar Ali with equal 8 annas share, for arrears of rent superior landlord obtained decree in rent suit without serving any notice and one Abdul Hakim shown to be auction purchaser. Abdul Hakim never obtained possession in pursuance of the decree passed in the rent suit. Dula Mia and his brother remained in possession of the suit property as before. Subsequently, Dula Mia filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for setting aside the auction and Abdul Hakim filed Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 against Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar Ali and their mother for possession of the auction purchased land. Both the suits were disposed of in accordance with solenama and in terms of solenama 45 decimals of land were given settlement in favour of Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia from RS Plot No.415. Abdul Hakim Majumder settled 96 decimals of land by way of unregistered patta dated 15-10-1948 in favour of Dula Mia at Selami of Taka 145 but in the patta wrongly RS Plot No.415 written and possession was given on RS Plot No.1246 in favour of Dula Mia. Dula Mia remained in possession of the property under plot No.1246 entirely and 8 annas share of land under plot No.3 and paid rents for schedule Nos. 1, 2, 4, 6 and for half share of RS Plot No.415 of schedule No. 3.

3. During Revisional settlement SA Khatian No.40 was prepared in the name of Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar. Dula Mia died leaving the plaintiffs as heirs and the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. Sekandar Ali, brother of Dula Mia remained in possession of schedule No. 3 and transferred the property under schedule Nos.7-9 in favour of the plaintiffs by registered deed dated 2-1-1976. The defendants have no manner right, title and interest in the suit land. The defendants claimed title on the suit land on 15-7-1988, hence the suit. Subsequently, the plaintiffs brought an amendment of the plaint on 14-6-1995 and claimed title on adverse possession.

4. The defendant Nos.1-3, 6, 11, 16, 20 and 24 entered appearance in the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit property under CS Khatian No.11 was auction sold and Abdul Hakim Majumder auction purchased the Jote under CS Khatian No.11 and got possession of the same excepting 7 decimals of land under plot No.360 and 13 decimals of land under Plot No. 361 and 4 decimals of land under Plot No. 365 total 24 decimals of land and for possession of which Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 in the Court of 3rd Munsif, Comilla against the predecessor of the plaintiffs Dula Mia and Sekandar Ali and others. The suit was disposed of in terms of Solenama with the defendant Nos.1-3, 15-18 of that suit. According to the terms of Solenama 45 decimals of land including 24 decimals of land was given settlement in favour of Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia for 5 years and after expiry of the said period since Dula Mia and his brother Sekandar Ali did not execute any Kabuliyat in favour of Abdul Hakim Majumder he filed Other Suit No. 92 of 1942 against them for recovery of possession of that land. In execution of that suit he got possession over the same on 7-2-1943.

5. Sekandar Ali and Dula Mia never got settlement of 45 decimals of land equally and possessed accordingly. Sekandar Ali filed objection under section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure against that execution case and that was dismissed on hearing and against that Appeal No.82 of 1943 was preferred by Sekandar Ali and that appeal was also disallowed on 17.08.1943. The claim of the plaintiff is that he obtained 96 decimals of land by way of patta dated 15-10-1948 is quite false and fictitious. Abdul Hakim Majumder never executed any patta deed in favour of Dula Mia. Plaintiff never obtained any suit property by way of Solenama and also did not obtain any property by registered deed dated 2-1-1976. The claim of the plaintiff is quite false and fictitious. The predecessor of the defendant Abdul Hakim obtained the suit property by auction purchase and obtained possession and during their possession the plaintiff and Sekandar Ali trespassed into the land comprising 19 decimals under plot Nos. 360 and 361 and subsequently got registered deed dated 25-6-1976 from the defendant No.1 and obtained possession of 6 decimals of land. Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Title Suit No.57 of 1988 for recovery of khas possession of 13 decimals of land in the court of Nangalkot and the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.

6. At the trial, the plaintiff adduced 3 PWs on the other hand, the defendant adduced 6 DWs and both the parties produced some documents which were marked as exhibits.

7. After hearing, the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla dismissed the suit of the plaintiff against which appeal was preferred which was also disallowed by the appellate court in Title Appeal No.196 of 1997.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree in dismissing the suit the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner preferred Revisional application before this court and obtained the present Rule.

9. At the time of hearing, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan with Mr Md Anwar Hossain, the learned Advocates appeared on behalf of the petitioners. On the other hand, Mr Md Israfil Hossain, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties.

10. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below, though dismissed the suit of the plaintiff with the concurrent findings that the plaintiffs could not prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence that they have title and possession in the suit land but this findings are based on non-consideration of the oral and documentary evidence on record which were marked as exhibits. Thus, the Judgment and decree passed by the Courts below are not based upon the proper appreciation of the evidence on record.

11. He further submits that the plaintiffs by adducing oral evidence proved plaint case that they are possessing the suit land and the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs were recorded in CS and SA Khatians in consideration of their physical possession in the suit land and the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land by paying rent and taxes to the authority since they are predecessors but the Courts below without proper perusal of the exhibits on record improperly found that the CS record was not prepared in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff which is a wrong findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below, thus, committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

12. He further submits that the Courts below in arriving a correct decision did not consider the aspect of the case, so far it relates to the documents produced by the plaintiffs which were kept safe custody of the Court but wrongly held that those documents were destroyed by the plaintiffs which is improbable, as the plaintiffs themselves produced those documents and it was the duty of the Court to take appropriate step to produce the same at the time of hearing and, as such, mis-directed the courts below on taking decisions on a wrong approach which mis-construed the total facts and circumstances of the case and thus, the courts below arrived at a wrong decision that the plaintiffs could not prove their case by producing documents before the Court.

13. He further submits that the courts below on mis-reading of the documents produced by the defendants wrongly found that the predecessor of the defendants were in possession in the suit land and they have got possession through process of law but the Courts below did not consider the documents which was produced by the plaintiff before the Court, though it was not marked as exhibit, yet from the report of the revenue officer it is apparent that the objection raised by the defendants was not accepted and Revenue Officer finding possession of the plaintiffs rejected the objection of the defendants and, as such, the findings of the Courts below that the defendants are in possession is not based on proper appreciation of the facts on record.

14. He also submits that the trial court found that the defendant-opposite parties admitted the possession of the plaintiff-petitioners on 12 acres of land but dismissed the suit as a whole without passing any decree as such both the courts below without applying judicial mind to the facts and circumstances of the case improperly passed the decree in dismissing the suit and committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

15. He further submits that after institution of the suit for declaration of title the plaintiff by way of amendment prayed for a decree by way of adverse possession and in support of their claim PW 1 in his deposition and cross-examination asserted that their predecessor was in possession of the suit land by way of settlement and patta and they are in possession also and as a whole they are in possession about 60 years in the suit land. Other P.Ws. corroborated the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 and thus the plaintiffs proved their case that they are in possession in the suit land since CS operation and it was proved by the report of the Revenue Officer that the objection raised by the defendants was rejected as such the plaintiffs have been able to prove their case. On the other hand, the defendants though produced some documents before the court but by adducing oral evidence they could not prove their possession in the suit land. Both the courts below on mis-appreciation of the facts and circumstances of the case mis-construed the same and arrived at a wrong decision in dismissing the suit of the plaintiff by which committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

16. On the other hand, Mr Md Israfil Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that the plaintiff-petitioners could not prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence on record before the trial court and the trial court on proper perusal of the evidence on record and the documents exhibited by the parties found that the plaintiffs have no title and possession over the suit land and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff. The appellate court affirmed the Judgment and decree passed by the trial court in dismissing the suit with proper appreciation of the facts and circumstances of the case and the documents on record. Thus, the appellate court committed no error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

17. He further submits that the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below cannot be interfered with by the Revisional jurisdiction as there is no mis-reading of the evidence on record which mis-construed the facts of the case. He also submits that the plaintiff-appellant-petitioners could not prove their case in producing the documents before the Court, though the documents were filed before the Court and it was kept in safe custody but those were not examined or exhibited in the Court because those were forged and fabricated documents and, as such, the Courts below found that the plaintiff could not prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence that they have any title and possession in the suit land.

18. He further submits that the defendants by adducing oral and documentary evidence prove their case that they have title and possession in the suit land, as they have got possession through Court, the defendant also established their claim that the alleged un-registered patta has no existence at all and on consideration of this fact both the Courts below found title and possession of the defendants in the suit land. So, the claim of the plaintiffs of adverse possession is not established in any form of evidence both oral and documentary and on consideration the aforesaid oral and documentary evidence of the trial court and the appellate court concurrently found that the defendants are in possession on the suit land and the plaintiffs have no title and possession on the suit land and dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. Thus, the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the Courts below cannot be interfered with by the Revisional jurisdiction in the facts and circumstances of the case. He prayed for discharged of the Rule.

19. Heard the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the Revisional application along with the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court as well as the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. I have also perused the lower courts records, the exhibits, the order sheets and other documents on record.

20. Title Suit No.132 of 1994 (re-numbered) was filed for declaration of title as well as adverse possession. The trial court framed 4 issues:-1) whether the suit is maintainable in its present form? 2) Whether the suit is barred by limitation? 3) Whether the plaintiffs have title over the suit land? 4) Whether the plaintiffs have possession in the suit land?

21. On perusal of the record it appears that the predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners namely Dula Mia and his brother namely Sekander Ali were the original owners of the suit land evidencing from the CS Khatian (Exhibit-1(Ka)) and RS Khatian (Exhbit-1). The predecessor of the Plaintiff-Petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 161 of 1939 for settlement. The predecessor of the Defendants-Opposite Parties No. 1-3 instituted Civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 for recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed on 11-10-1939 on Solenama (Exhibit-2) according to Solenama, 0.45 acre were settled to Dula Mia and Sekender Ali. As per terms of Solenama Suit land was settled to Dula Mia vide registered patta dated 15-10-1948 and Partly Settlement Khatian No. 151 was recorded for Dula Mia and after SAT Act coming into force, Dula Mia became owner of the Suit land under the Government and RS Khatian (Exhibit-1) was recorded in the name of Dula Mia and he paid rents (Exhibit-3 series).

22. The suit land was put in auction and the predecessor of the defendants-opposite party Nos.1-3 namely Abdul Hakim auction purchased the suit land. On prayer of the predecessor of the petitioner namely Dula Mia, Abdul Hakim settled 96 acres schedule land vide registered patta dated 15-10-1948 in favour of the Dula Mia from CS Plot Nos. 363, 365, 415, 418, 329, 327.

23. CS Khatian [Exhibit-1(Ka)] No.11 shows the record and possession of Sakander Ali and Dula Mia sons of Bande Ali to the extent of 4(four) anna share in the entire land recorded in the khatian. SA Khatian (Exhibit No.1) No. 40 shows the record of right in various plots in the name of Sekander Ali and Dula Mia.

24. The plaintiffs pleaded adverse possession in Title Suit No. 118 of 1988 (present suit) in paragraph No.5 as follows:

“দুলা মিয়া বর্ণিত মতে বন্দোবস্ত মূলে নিজ স্বত্ব প্রচারে অন্যের স্বত্ব অস্বীকারে অন্যের বিরুদ্ধে দখল জনিত স্বত্বে তপছিলোক্ত ভূমিতে মালিক দখলকার বিদ্যমান থাকিয়া তাহাতে নিয়মিত ফসলাদি সৃজনে ভোগ তছরুপ করতে থাকে।”

25. In paragraph No.6 the plaintiffs also pleaded adverse possession as follows:

“বাদীগণ পূর্ববর্তীক্রমে বিগত ৪৬/৪৭ বৎসর যাবত নিজ স্বত্ব প্রচারে অপরের স্বত্ব অস্বীকারে বিবাদীগণ ও তাহাদের পূর্ববর্তীগণের নিজ নিজ দখল জনিত স্বত্বে মালিক দখলকার বিদ্যমান আছে।”

26. The plaintiffs by filing an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure sought amendment of the plaint of follows:

“(ক) আরজির শিরোনামে মোকদ্দমা শব্দের পর বিরুদ্ধে দখলজনিত স্বত্বে রায়তী স্বত্ব লিপি হইবে (খ) আরজির ৯ম দফায় (ক) প্রার্থনায় বাদীগণ শব্দের পর বিরুদ্ধে দখল জনিত স্বত্বে রায়তী শব্দ লিপি হইবে।”

27. The trial court as well as the lower appellate court misread the oral and documentary evidence and did not consider material evidence.

(i) Trial Court in the judgment at Page-65 of the Civil Revision found that “বাদীগণ এর দাখিলী ৪০ নং হাল খতিয়ানের জাবেদা নকল প্রদর্শনী-১ দ্বারা এই বিষয় সমর্থিত যে দুলা মিয়া তাহার ওয়ারেশদের নামে নালিশী ভূমি রেকর্ড হয় নাই।”

This is misreading of evidence. Ext. 1, SA Khatian No. 40, which shows that the names of Sekander Ali and Dula Mia have been recorded in the Khatian. (ii) The finding of the trial court with regard to the possession of the party is not based on consideration of material oral and documentary evidence. The plaintiffs' witnesses in their deposition proved the possession of the plaintiffs. The documentary evidence shows that possession was not taken from the predecessor of the plaintiffs at any point of time by the predecessor of the defendants.

(i) The compromise petition filed in civil Suit No. 19 of 1939 shows that possession remained with the plaintiff's predecessor.

(ii) Patta dated 15-10-1948 shows that it was executed in terms of the sole decree.

(iii) The ownership, possession and also settlement patta of 96 decimals of land in favour of Dula Mia were proved by petty settlement khatian 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the Khatian.

(iv) The dismissal of the suit being Title Suit No. 57 of 1988 filed by the defendant-predecessors for recovery of possession of 13 decimals of land of plot o. 361 appertaining khatian No. 40 for the predecessor of the plaintiffs shows that possession remained with plaintiff predecessor. (v) The successors of Abdul Hakim Majumder i.e. the defendants in the present suit filed objection under Rule 30 of the Tenancy rules against record of rights in the name of the plaintiffs and for correcting the record in the name of the defendants. The Revenue Officer by an order dated 06-8-1990 dismissed the objection with the finding as follows:

“বিরোধীয় জমি বাড়ী ও কবরস্থান। পিতা চাচাগণের আমলে বাড়ী সৃজন করা হইয়াছে। আজও বসবাস করিতেছেন। পূর্ব পূরুষের বহু কবর বিরোধীয় দাগে আছে জানান এস. এ ৫২ নং খতিয়ানে এস. এ রেকর্ড আছে জানান। বিরোধীয় জমি নিলামে খরিদ্দার হিসাবে মোকদ্দমার ডিক্রীমূলে মালিক দাবী কালীণ ও বিরোধীয় দাগে বিবাদীপক্ষ পূর্ব পুরুষের আমল থেকে বাড়ী ও কবর সৃজন করিয়া এস.এ রেকর্ড করাইয়া ভোগ দখলে আছেন বিধায় আপত্তিকারী পক্ষেও নাম রেকর্ড দেওয়া গেলনা। অতএব আদেশ হয় আপত্তিকারী পক্ষেও দাবী নামঞ্জুর।”

The above order clearly established the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land from the time of their predecessor. (vi) PW 1 deposed in the suit that Abdus Hakim Majumder could not go into possession of the suit land. Plaintiff in their pleading claimed adverse possession. PW 1 in his deposition claimed decree on the basis of adverse possession PW 2 deposed that plaintiffs and their predecessor have been possessing the suit land and that defendants never possessed the suit land and never evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land PW 3 corroborated PWs 1 and 2 in respect of plaintiffs and their predecessor's possession in the suit land. The oral and documentary evidence conclusively proves that the plaintiff-predecessors were in possession of the suit land since the time of CS record and possession was not ever taken from them by the predecessor of the defendants and the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land from the time of their predecessors. The trial court and the lower appellate Court have misread the evidence, oral and documentary and did not consider oral and documentary evidence while dismissing the suit filed by the plaintiffs. (vii) The unregistered patta executed by Abdul Hakim Majumder filed by the plaintiff was kept in safe custody where damaged the same, but the lower appellate court has drawn an adverse inference against the plaintiffs most arbitrarily to the effect that the damage was caused by the plaintiffs without considering that nobody will take any action to destroy his own evidence and this shows that the lower appellant court failed to apply its judicial mind to the facts of this case.

28. The decree passed in Civil Suit No.19 of 1939 between Abdul Hakim Majumder and Sekander Ali and Dula Mia and other shows that the suit was decreed on the basis of Solenama and that the plaintiff in that suit namely Abdul Hakim Majumder agreed to give settlement of 45 decimals of land defendant Nos. 1 and 2 namely Sekander Ali and Dula Mia. The compromise petition shows that Sekander Ali and Dula Mia were in possession of 45 decimals of land.

29. The patta executed by Abdul Hakim Majumder (defendants predecessor) in favour of Dula Mia, son of Late Bande Ali (plaintiff's predecessor) shows that about Hakim Majumder executed patta dated 15-10-1948 settling 96 decimals of land in favour of the Dula Mia according to the terms of sole decree in civil Suit No. 19 of 1939. The ownership, and possession and also settlement of Dula Mia in 96 decimals of land are also evidenced from the petty settlement Khatian No. 11/1 recording the name of Dula Mia in the khatian.

30. AK Fazlul Haque Majumder, son of late Abdul Hakim Majumder filed Title Suit No. 57 of 1988 against Ayub Ali and others sons of Dula Mia in the court of Assistant Judge, Nangolkot, Comilla for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of 13 decimals of land in plot no. 361 appertaining to khatian No.40 (part of the suit land) which was contested by the defendant in that suit by filing written statement denying the material allegation in the plaint. The plaintiff of that suit did not proceed with the suit as a result the suit was dismissed due to absence of the plaintiff, Ext. Ka/5(Kha) vide order dated 21-9-1991 of the learned Assistant Judge, Nangolkot, Comilla.

31. In the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216, in Paragraph-8 it has been held: "Plaintiffs name has also been recorded in SA Khatian and all objections raised by defendant No.1 were overruled by the Revenue office"

32. In the present case also the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs were recorded in the CS and SA Khatian and objection filed by the defendant-predecessors against the record in the name of the plaintiff-predecessors was rejected. This shows the possession of the plaintiffs and their predecessor in the suit land.

33. In the Case reported in 54 DLR (AD) 173 relying on the case reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287 and other decisions it has been held by our Apex Court "Since the receipt is not a document of title it could not canter title to the plaintiff under the provisions of section 54 of the Transfer of Property Act but the uninterrupted adverse and hostile possession of the plaintiff over a period of 12 years The plaintiff has acquired title by adverse possession.

34. Then in paragraph 10 it has been held by Appellate Division as follows: "Thus when there is an invalid transfer in favour of a person and he holds possession of the property transferred as transferee, his possession is in his own right and adverse to the transferor. If he continues in possession of immovable property for more that twelve years he will acquire an indefeasible title.

35. After considering the decisions in several cases the Appellate Division came to the following conclusion: "Thus the courts below on misreading of evidence on record and on misconception of law as aforesaid wrongly held that elements constituting adverse possession are lacking in the case and most illegally dismissed the suit by the impugned judgment and accordingly, the suit succeeds and the impugned judgment of the High court Division affirming those of the courts below are set aside and the suit is decreed without any order as to cost."

36. In the present case if it is found that the patta granting settlement in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor is defective then in view of continues adverse possession of the plaintiffs from their predecessors for more than 60 years prior to the institution of the suit as evidenced form the rent receipts and oral and documentary evidence has conferred indefeasible title on the plaintiffs.

37. In the case reported in 6 MLR (AD) 257 the Appellate Division in paragraph held; "The court of appeal below on consideration of the evidence on record held that in view of the possession of the plaintiffs since 1926 ad that Jogendra did not transfer the property for and on behalf of Ananda, the minor and thus the transfer was invalid one and that it is proved on admitted evidence that the plaintiffs are in possession of the disputed properties for more than 12 years before the institution of the suit and that Baisnab was in possession all along and that the plaintiffs were in possession on the date of the filing of the suit and was also in possession for more than 12 years before the institution of the suit and thus perfected their title in respect of the suit properties by adverse possession against the defendants and all others."

38. In the present case the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession and their predecessors' possession since the time of CS record and hence, even if there is any defect in the transfer of title to the plaintiffs they are entitled to declaration of title by adverse possession of more than 60 years of the date of the institution of the suit.

39. In the case reported in 16 BLD (AD) 197 = 48 DLR (AD) 160 the Appellate Division held: "The High Court Division was wrong in refusing to exercise its Revisional jurisdiction in the case where due to non-consideration of the material evidence on record an erroneous decision was arrived at occasioning a grave failure of justice."

40. In the case reported in 18 DLR 107 (Paragraph-7) it has been held as follows:

"An agreement to lease immovable property from year to year or for any term exceeding one year accompanied by delivery of possession in the absence of registered lease deed, is valid for one year, and if the lessee continues in possession with assent of the lessor, the lessee becomes a tenant by holding over under section 116 of the TP Act."

<u>41. In the present case, since the unregistered patta was accompanied by delivery of possession the lease is valid for one year and the plaintiffs and their predecessors having continued in possession with the assent of the lessor the plaintiffs became tenants by holding over under section 116 of the Transfer of property Act. So even if the unregistered patta is treated as lease for one year, lease continued by the possession of the plaintiffs and their predecessors and therefore, they became tenants in the suit land by holding over under section 116 of the Transfer of property Act. Hence, the settlement in favour of the plaintiffs' predecessor is valid and the plaintiffs being in lawful possession has acquired title in the suit land.</u>

42. In the present case both the trial court and the lower appellate court arrived at their decisions without considering material evidence and by misreading the material evidence and on misconception of law and hence, the High Court Division in exercising of its Revisional jurisdiction is competent to interfere with the concurrent findings.

43. In the case reported in 40 DLR (AD) 62 the Appellate Division held in paragraph 15 as follows:

"Mr Rafiq-ul-Huq lastly contends that both the trial court and the appellate court came to a concurrent finding that the balance of convenience lies in favour of the appellant and that he is the highest bidder, this finding is immune from interference in revision by the High Court Division. But in view of the facts discussed above we find that the very basis of the findings of the two courts below is a misconception as to which tenders are relevant in the suit. As such the concurrent finding cannot claim any immunity."

44. In view of the principle laid down in the above decision, the concurrent findings in this case cannot claim any immunity and is liable to be interfered with in revision.

45. In the case reported in 11 BLT (AD) 60 the Appellate Division held in paragraph 4 as follows:

"We find no substance in the submission. It is well settled that once the conditions in section 115(1) of the code of civil procedure are satisfied and the High Court's jurisdiction to interfere is established, the proceedings as a whole from start to finish can be scrutinized and any order necessary for doing justice may be passed. There is no limit to the area in which the Revisional power is to be exercised by the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of each case."

46. In view of the principle laid down in the above case, the High Court Division can interfere in this case in Revisional jurisdiction.

47. In Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2703 of 2010 the Appellate Division has held, inter alia, as follows: "The learned Counsel has argued that this deed of agreement for re-convenience was duly placed before the trial court for the proper custody and sufficient evidence was also adduced to prove the execution of this deed of agreement and in the circumstances the mere non-marking of this deed as exhibit by the court cannot be any reason for not taking this deed into consideration by the Courts below. The learned Counsel has contended that the non-making of this agreement deed as exhibit is a mere mistake made by the Court and for this mistake of the court the party who adduced this document before the Court and gave sufficient evidence necessary for marking it as exhibit cannot suffer."

48. In the present case the order passed by the Revenue Officer on 6-8-1990 finding the plaintiffs' possession was filed in Court but the same was not marked exhibit for which the plaintiffs are not responsible. Hence, this order ought to have been taken into consideration by the courts below.

49. In view of the infirmity as found in the judgments of the Court below for misreading and non-consideration of the evidence on record and in view of the principles of law laid down by the Apex Court of the country as referred to herein before, I am of the opinion that this is an appropriate case for interference by the High Court Division in Revisional jurisdiction.

50. From the discussions made above and the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, the order sheet of the trial court and other documents produced before the Court, it appears that the plaintiffs have title and possession in the suit land and they have also acquired title by way of adverse possession in the suit land, since they are enjoying uninterrupted possession in the suit land and CS Record and SA Record and rent receipts and the order of the Revenue Officer in the mutation case proved the aforesaid claim of the plaintiffs. Thus, the Courts below committed an error of law in dismissing the suit of the plaintiffs which occasioned a failure of justice. Thus, the Rule succeeds.

51. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

52. The impugned judgment and decree dated 11-9-2006 passed by the District Judge, Comilla in Title Appeal No.196 of 1997 affirming the judgment and decree dated 24-8-1997 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Comilla in Civil Suit No.132 of 1994 are set aside. Accordingly, the title suit No. 132 of 1994 is decreed.

Send down the lower court records along with a copy of this Judgment to the trial Court at once.
